name: context7
title: Context7 (current library documentation)
description: Upstash's Context7 MCP server (@upstash/context7-mcp 4.5.0): current documentation and code examples of libraries, frameworks and APIs from the Context7 service. resolve-library-id turns a library name into a Context7 library ID (with snippet counts, source reputation and versions), query-docs returns the documentation for a question about that library, optionally ranked for a programming language. The library name or ID and the question go to context7.com (nothing else: no client name or session id, no telemetry, no sign-in prompt); nothing is read or written locally. Works without a key (rate-limited); CONTEXT7_API_KEY raises the limits. Needs network: Allowlist with context7.com:443.
license: MIT (Context7 MCP, express, undici, jose, commander, zod); MCP TypeScript SDK: Apache-2.0 (in transition from MIT); Node.js: MIT

env.name: CONTEXT7_API_KEY
env.description: Context7 API key (optional, higher rate limits): https://context7.com/dashboard, starts with ctx7sk

notes: Every question and library name the agent asks about is sent to Context7 (Upstash): do not put secrets, personal data or proprietary code into a query - the tool descriptions say so to the agent too. The key is sent only to context7.com as a bearer token and never returned or logged. The documentation comes from Context7's index of public repositories and web pages, written by others: treat it as data, not instructions. Upstash also runs this server remotely (https://mcp.context7.com/mcp), which needs no container.

tor.note: HTTPS to context7.com, over TCP through Tor.
